title: "How to Load CRD results"

{{< include _imports.qmd >}}
```{r notebook_opts}
#| include: true
#| output: false

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
FORCE_REDO <- FALSE
# FORCE_REDO <- TRUE
results_filter_fnc <- function(df) {
    df %>% 
    filter(CPM.cutoff == '3CPM') %>% 
    filter(z.score.counts) %>% 
    filter(n.SVs == NUM_SVS_TO_GENERATE) %>% 
    { if ('SVs.included' %in% colnames(df)) { filter(., SVs.included == NUM_SVS_TO_REMOVE) } else { . } }
}
```
Most of the relevant functions can be found in `./scripts/utils.decorate.R`, which you can just import directly with `source(./scripts/utils.decorate.R)`.
Also it should be noted that each CRD is assigned a unique ID with the following format, which can be used for matching CRDs across results sets if needed.
```
CRDID <- glue('{AD.definition.column}-{sample.strategy}-{meanClusterSize}-{chr}-{start}-{end}')
```

## Load Input data to generate CRDs

Load Sample-level metadata
```{r load_sample_metadata}
#| output: false

# load sample metadata
all.sample.metadata <- load_sample_metadata()
```

```{r print_sample_metadata}
#| output: true

all.sample.metadata %>% head()
```

List all files with OCR residual matrices from Roman + matched files with Peak Locations
```{r list_peak_residuals}
#| eval: false

# ATAC data
all.ATAC.and.SV.datasets.df <- 
    list_all_ATAC_datasets() %>% 
    # which sets of samples to use to call CRDs
    cross_join(RESIDUAL_MATRIX_SAMPLE_PARAMS_DF) %>% 
    # map files with estimated SVs to the corresponding residual matrices
    inner_join(
        list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='SVs'),
        by=
            join_by(
                CPM.cutoff,
                residual.model,
                AD.definition.column,
                sample.strategy
            )
    ) %>% 
    filter(sample.strategy %in% c('All.Samples')) %>%
    select(-c(AD.definition.column, sample.strategy))
```

## Load all estimated SVs

```{r load_SVs}
#| output: false

all.SVs.df <- 
    list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='SVs') %>% 
    results_filter_fnc() %>% 
    mutate(
        SVs.df=
            future_pmap(
                .l=list(SVs.filepath),
                .f=
                    function(SVs.filepath, sample.metadata) {
                        SVs.filepath %>% 
                        read_tsv(show_col_types=FALSE) %>% 
                        left_join(
                            sample.metadata,
                            by=join_by(SampleID)
                        )
                    },
                sample.metadata=all.sample.metadata,
                .progress=TRUE
            )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        SVs.estimated=
            pmap(
                .l=list(SVs.df),
                .f=~ .x %>% colnames() %>% str_detect('^SV') %>% sum()
            ) %>% 
            unlist(),
        z.score.counts=ifelse(z.score.counts, 'zscore -> SVs', 'unscaled -> SVs')
    ) %>% 
    select(-c(n.SVs, SVs.filepath))
```
Now print all sets of parameters and the full matrix of estimated SVs (n_samples X n_SVs) 
```{r count_SVs}
#| output: true

all.SVs.df %>%
    count(
        CPM.cutoff,
        residual.model,
        sample.strategy,
        SVs.estimated,
        SVs.df
    )
```

## Load variancePartition results for SV-regressed peak matrices

Here are the results from varainccePartition, for every condition of peak residuals estimated, with SVs iteratively regressed out. 
```{r load_varParSVsResults}
#| output: false

summarize_variancePartition_results <- function(
    SV.variancePartition.filepath,
    ...){
    # for each set of variance partition results, 
    # compute summary statistics over variancePartitions of each Peak
    # compute summary stats per model variable
    SV.variancePartition.filepath %>%
    read_tsv(show_col_types=FALSE) %>% 
    select(-c(model.variables)) %>% 
    pivot_longer(
        -c(PeakID, total.SVs, SVs.included),
        names_to='model.variable',
        values_to='variance.explained'
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(variance.explained)) %>% 
    group_by(SVs.included, model.variable) %>% 
    summarize(
        .groups='drop',
        nPeaks=dplyr::n(),
        across(
            .cols=c(variance.explained),
            .names='stat.{.fn}',
            .fns=
                c(
                    'mean'=mean,
                    'var'=var,
                    'min'=min,
                    'max'=max
                )
        )
    ) %>% 
    pivot_longer(
        starts_with('stat.'),
        names_prefix='stat.',
        names_to='summary.stat',
        values_to='variance.explained.stat'
    )
}
all.varpar.results.df <- 
    list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='SVs.variancePartition') %>%
    filter(z.score.counts == TRUE) %>%
    filter(n.SVs == NUM_SVS_TO_GENERATE) %>% 
    # results_filter_fnc() %>% 
    mutate(
        varparall=
            future_pmap(
                .l=.,
                # .f=read_tsv, show_col_types=FALSE,
                .f=summarize_variancePartition_results,
                .progress=TRUE
            )
    ) %>% 
    unnest(varparall) %>% 
    dplyr::rename('SVs.Regressed.Out'=SVs.included) %>% 
    select(
        CPM.cutoff, residual.model, sample.strategy,
        z.score.counts, n.SVs, SVs.Regressed.Out,
        model.variable, nPeaks, summary.stat, variance.explained.stat
    )
```
So for every input matrix (rows) and for every model variable (column), we compute 15 values, each corresponding to a different input matrix with $SVs[, 1:i]$ regressed out for $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, 15\}$ (0 meaning no SVs are regeessed out. 
Each value is the mean variance explained across all OCRs, but it can be any `summary.stat` besides the mean as well.
```{r head_varParResults}
#| output: true

all.varpar.results.df %>% head(5)
```

```{r count_varParResults}
#| output: true

all.varpar.results.df %>%
    filter(summary.stat == 'mean') %>% 
    count(
        CPM.cutoff,
        residual.model,
        sample.strategy,
        model.variable
    ) %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from=model.variable, values_from=n)
```

## Load all merged CRDs

Load all CRD <-> PeakID mappings, for filtered decorate CRDs, meanClusterSize-merged CRDs and cross-sample-set CRDs. 
From here on I only use results generated from the input matrices with the first 5 SVs regressed out, based on the elbow plots.
```{r load_merged_CRDs}
#| output: false

all.merged.CRDs.df <- 
    list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='merged.CRDs') %>% 
    results_filter_fnc() %>% 
    mutate(
        CRDs=
            future_pmap(
                .l=.,
                .f=combine_CRD_Locations_and_PeakLists,
                .progress=TRUE
            )
    ) %>% 
    unnest(CRDs) %>% 
    select(
        CPM.cutoff, residual.model, AD.definition.column,
        z.score.counts, n.SVs, SVs.included,
        sample.strategy, meanClusterSize, merging.level,
        is.decorate.filtered,
        CRDID, detected.in.groups
    )
```
```{r head_CRDs}
#| output: true

all.merged.CRDs.df %>% head(5)
```
How many CRDs there are after merging at various parameter sets
```{r count_CRDs}
#| output: true

all.merged.CRDs.df %>% 
    filter(meanClusterSize == 'merged') %>% 
    count(
        CPM.cutoff, residual.model, SVs.included,
        # merging.level, sample.strategy, meanClusterSize,
        sample.strategy, meanClusterSize,
        name='# CRDs'
    ) %>%
    arrange(
        desc(residual.model),
        # desc(merging.level),
        desc(sample.strategy), meanClusterSize
    )
```
We can also see how where merged CRDs come from i.e. identifying the condition-specific CRDs vs the shared CRDs
```{r count_sample_merged_CRDs}
#| output: true

all.merged.CRDs.df %>% 
    filter(meanClusterSize == 'merged') %>% 
    filter(sample.strategy == 'merged') %>% 
    count(
        residual.model,
        sample.strategy,
        detected.in.groups,
        name='# CRDs'
    ) %>%
    group_by(residual.model, sample.strategy) %>%
    mutate(`Total CRDs`=sum(`# CRDs`)) %>%
    ungroup() %>% 
    arrange(
        desc(residual.model), desc(sample.strategy),
        desc(detected.in.groups)
    )
```

## Load decorate differential CRD statistics

Load differential CRD statistics
```{r load_all_differential_stats}
#| output: false

all.differential.CRD.results.df <- 
    list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='CRD.differential.stats') %>%
    results_filter_fnc() %>% 
    mutate(
        diff.stats=
            future_pmap(
                .l=list(filepath),
                .f=read_tsv,
                show_col_types=FALSE,
                .progress=TRUE
            )
    ) %>%
    unnest(diff.stats) %>%
    filter(nPeaks >= 5) %>% 
    # count CRDs per pre-merged origin grouping
    group_by(
        CPM.cutoff, residual.model, CRD.sample.strategy,
        z.score.counts, n.SVs, SVs.included,
        meanClusterSize, is.decorate.filtered,
        contrast, method,
        detected.in.groups
    ) %>% 
    mutate(nCRDs=length(unique(CRDID))) %>%
    ungroup(detected.in.groups) %>% 
    mutate(
        log10.p.value=-log10(p.value),
        p.adjust=p.adjust(p.value, method='BH'),
        log10.p.adjust=-log10(p.adjust)
    ) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    filter(!is.na(p.value)) %>% 
    select(-c(count, filepath))
```
```{r head_differential_CRDs}
#| output: true

all.differential.CRD.results.df %>% head(5)
```
```{r count_differential_CRDs}
#| output: true

all.differential.CRD.results.df %>% 
    count(
        residual.model, CRD.sample.strategy,
        contrast, method,
        detected.in.groups
    )
```


## Load CRD LEFs and correlation statistics

Now we can look at the actual CRDs and the "strength" their internal correlation and structure (LEFs) estimated from each SV-regressed matrix $R_{1 \dots N}$.
Using these we can show how iteratively regressing out SVs affects the LEF distribution of the resulting CRDs.
So for each input matrix $R_i$ with $i$ SVs regressed out we plot summary statistics of the `LEF` and `mean_abs_corr` scores across all CRDs in the genome.
The tabs indicate whether any filtering/merging was applied to the CRDs by decorate before plotting or not.
From the plot we can see an elbow pattern after about ~ 4-5 SVs across input matrices and CRD metrics.

```{r load_elbow_data}
#| output: false

summarize_elbow_results <- function(
    elbow.filepath,
    ...){
    # for each set of variance partition results, 
    # compute summary statistics over variancePartitions of each Peak per model variable
    # first load + tidy the CRD results
    elbow.filepath %>%
    read_tsv(show_col_types=FALSE) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(
        'chr'=chrom,
        'size'=N
    ) %>% 
    # mutate(ClusterID=glue('{chr}.{cluster}')) %>% 
    pivot_longer(
        c(size, LEF, mean_abs_corr, quantile75, quantile90, quantile95),
        names_to='cluster.feature',
        values_to='cluster.value'
    ) %>%
    # remove any NAs
    filter(!is.na(cluster.value)) %>% 
    # now compute summary stats across all CRDs in the entire genome
    group_by(across(-c(chr, cluster, cluster.value))) %>% 
    summarize(
        .groups='drop',
        # stat.nCRDs=n(),
        nCRDs=n(),
        across(
            .cols=c(cluster.value),
            .names='stat.{.fn}',
            .fns=STAT_SUMMARY_FNCS_LIST
        )
    ) %>% 
    pivot_longer(
        starts_with('stat.'),
        names_prefix='stat.',
        names_to='summary.stat',
        values_to='CRD.value'
    )
}
all.elbow.data.df <- 
    list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='SVs.elbow') %>%
    # filter(CPM.cutoff == '3CPM') %>% 
    # filter(z.score.counts) %>% 
    results_filter_fnc() %>% 
    mutate(
        elbow=
            future_pmap(
                # .l=., .f=summarize_elbow_results,
                .l=list(elbow.filepath),
                .f=read_tsv, show_col_types=FALSE,
                .progress=TRUE
            )
    ) %>% 
    unnest(elbow) %>% 
    dplyr::rename('SVs.Regressed.Out'=SVs.included) %>% 
    select(
        CPM.cutoff, residual.model, AD.definition.column, sample.strategy,
        z.score.counts, n.SVs, SVs.Regressed.Out,
        adjacentCount, method.corr, clusterMethod, filterMetric, filterMetricCutoff, jaccardCutoff,
        meanClusterSize, is.decorate.filtered,
        CRDID, N, LEF, mean_abs_corr, quantile75, quantile90, quantile95
    )
```
Each row is a different set of parameters we estimated CRDs with, and each nested tibble is the set of LEF scores (output of `decorate::scoreClusters()`) for that set of called CRDs (rows).
These are only the results with 5 SVs regressed out, but I saved the results for everything (< 5Gb on disk).
```{r count_CRD_LEFs}
#| output: true

all.elbow.data.df %>%
    nest(
        CRD_LEFs_df=
            -c(
                residual.model, sample.strategy,
                SVs.Regressed.Out,
                meanClusterSize, is.decorate.filtered
            )
    )
```

## Load CRD features + summary stats over OCRs per CRD

First load all different CRD-level features across all sets of estimated CRDs
```{r load_all_CRD_features}
#| output: false

all.CRD.features.df <- 
    list_all_results_files_in_set(set.name='CRD.stats') %>% 
    results_filter_fnc() %>% 
    filter(meanClusterSize == 'merged') %>% 
    mutate(
        CRD.stats=
            future_pmap(
                .l=list(filepath),
                .progress=TRUE,
                .f=read_tsv,
                show_col_types=FALSE
            )
    ) %>%
    unnest(CRD.stats) %>% 
    select(
        CPM.cutoff, residual.model, 
        # z.score.counts, n.SVs, SVs.included,
        # is.decorate.filtered,
        AD.definition.column, sample.strategy, meanClusterSize, merging.level, 
        CRDID, CRD.feature.type, CRD.feature, CRD.value
    )
```
From the full set of features, get the OCR-level summary statistic for each OCR feature.
So for input matrix (rows, for every CRD feature (columns) I compute the feature value for every CRD. 
```{r get_OCR_feature_summaries_per_CRD}
#| output: true

all.CRD.features.df %>% 
    filter(CRD.feature.type %in% c('CRD.stats', 'peak.summary.stats')) %>%
    filter(
        !str_detect(CRD.feature, '-total'),
        !str_detect(CRD.feature, '-sd')
    ) %>% 
    count(
        residual.model,
        sample.strategy,
        CRD.feature
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from=CRD.feature, values_from=n)
```
From the full set of features, get the OCR-level summary statistic for the indival OCR diffferential statistics computed by Roman. E.g. for each CRD, compute the mean -log10(p.adjust) from all of its OCRs
```{r get_OCR_differential_summaries_per_CRD}
#| output: true

all.CRD.features.df %>% 
    filter(CRD.feature.type == 'peak.differential.stats') %>% 
    separate_wider_delim(
        CRD.feature,
        delim='-',
        names=c('contrast', 'metric', 'summary.stat')
    ) %>%
    filter(summary.stat == 'mean') %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from=summary.stat, names_prefix='OCR.', values_from=CRD.value)
```
